question: What is the estimated cost of reconstruction needs for Ukraine's energy infrastructure? (Ước tính thiệt hại tái thiết cơ sở hạ tầng năng lượng Ukraine là bao nhiêu?)

gold.evidence:
Attacks to Ukraine’s energy infrastructure have created an estimated $91 billion 
in reconstruction needs.

results.text:
In March, the World Bank released the updated Rapid Damage and Needs 
Assessment for Ukraine, which emphasized the need for both public and private 
funds to address an estimated $411 billion in reconstruction and recovery costs over 
the next 10 years. The highest estimated needs are in transport, housing, energy, 
social protection and livelihoods, explosive-hazard management, and agriculture.

Attacks to Ukraine’s energy infrastructure have created an estimated $91 billion 
in reconstruction needs. The World Bank Group is supporting the Government of 
Ukraine to develop a European Union (EU)-aligned energy sector strategy to restore 
security of supply, reestablish financial viability, mobilize private capital at scale, 
strengthen corporate governance of state energy companies, and improve financial 
sustainability — essential ingredients for economic competitiveness, productivity, and 
employment creation.

52 THE WORLD BANK ANNUAL REPORT 2023
Ensuring access to sustainable energy for all 
Energy-related emissions account for over 75 percent of global emissions. The war on 
Ukraine has led to volatile energy prices and supply worldwide, particularly affecting 
the poorest countries. This crisis has highlighted the urgent need to deploy renew-
able energy on a massive scale to mitigate climate change and ensure energy reliabil-
ity and security. T echnological advances have greatly reduced the cost of renewable 
energy, presenting an opportunity to increase its share in the global energy mix.

question: Why is water security essential for Jordan's economy according to the 2024 report? (Tại sao an ninh nguồn nước là cốt lõi cho kinh tế Jordan?)

gold.evidence:
Water security is foundational for productivity and economic growth. As one 
of the most water-scarce countries in the world, Jordan has struggled to

results.text:
Water security is foundational for productivity and economic growth. As one 
of the most water-scarce countries in the world, Jordan has struggled to grow 
its economy and create jobs for its young people. The government of Jordan is taking bold action to boost water security by 
initiating its largest-ever infrastructure project, the Aqaba-Amman Water 
Desalination and Conveyance Project. By 2030, the project is expected 
to deliver approximately 40 percent of Jordan’s domestic water supply.

Complementing the Aqaba-Amman project is IBRD’s $300 million Jordan 
Water Sector Efficiency Project, which includes financing from partners. This 
is strengthening Jordan’s broader water sector through non-revenue water 
reduction, energy efficiency, and distribution-system readiness. The World Bank Group’s support for Jordan’s water sector aligns with our 
Water Strategy Implementation Plan, which outlines how investments, 
long-term policy reforms, and institutional sustainability can deliver water 
security, economic growth, and job creation.

64 THE WORLD BANK ANNUAL REPORT 2023
Ensuring water security for people and the planet
T oday, over 2 billion people lack safe drinking water, 3.6 billion people lack safe san-
itation, and at least 1.8 billion people face significant flood risk. With 70 percent of 
the world’s water shared across national boundaries and the variability of trans -
boundary water resources due to climate change, risks of water-induced conflicts 
are escalating.

question: What role does the World Bank serve regarding Financial Intermediary Funds (FIFs)? (Ngân hàng Thế giới đóng vai trò gì đối với các Quỹ FIFs?)

gold.evidence:
Financial intermediary funds (FIFs) represent large, 
distinct, multi-partner financing arrangements, for 
which the World Bank provides administrative support.

results.text:
FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARY FUNDS 
Financial intermediary funds (FIFs) represent large, 
distinct, multi-partner financing arrangements, for 
which the World Bank provides administrative support. They enable the international community to pool 
and coordinate funding from many sources to tackle 
specific development challenges, such as disease, 
food security, and other systemic changes. FIFs are 
independently governed, and the World Bank Group 
has no decision-making authority.

Instead, FIFs rely on 
the World Bank to provide financial and other services 
to facilitate their funding efforts and decisions. The 
World Bank serves as trustee for 27 FIFs. At the end of 
fiscal 2026, $45.2 billion was held in trust in the form

question: According to the 2023 report, how does gender equality impact development in Western and Central Africa? (Bình đẳng giới tác động thế nào tới phát triển ở Tây và Trung Phi năm 2023?)

gold.evidence:
Gender equality is not only essential for building more inclusive societies, but it 
can also accelerate progress in other areas of development, from improving human 
capital and food security to addressing climate change

results.text:
THE RE GIONS 23
Empowering women and girls in Western and 
Central Africa
Gender equality is not only essential for building more inclusive societies, but it 
can also accelerate progress in other areas of development, from improving human 
capital and food security to addressing climate change and fragility. But despite 
progress, women and girls in Western and Central Africa have a 58 percent chance 
of not being enrolled in secondary school and a 20 percent chance of bearing chil-
dren as a teenager. Regardless of the sector in which they work, they can expect to 
earn less than men.

But across the continent, the program is attract -
ing more and more female students for whom “science has no gender. ” Currently, 
about 35 percent of students enrolled in the program across Africa are women. Our work with countries to advance gender equality is showing strong results. According to the World Bank’s most recent Women, Business, and the Law report, 
Gabon and Côte d’Ivoire were among the top reformers in Sub-Saharan Africa, 
increasing their index scores from 82.5 to 95 and from 83.1 to 95, respectively.

They are helping close gaps in earnings and 
economic opportunity, reduce gender-based violence, and afford women and girls’ 
voice and agency. Guided by our regional gender action plan for Western and Central 
Africa, the Bank will continue to work with countries across the region to drive trans-
formational change on the scale that women and girls deserve in order to ensure all 
people are able to achieve their full potential. Spotlight

he world is facing myriad global challenges—including climate change, 
pandemics, and conflict. At the same time, many developing countries

alized people. These crises threaten hard-won gains in human capital, economic 
empowerment, and voice and agency.
